method.nvdla_spec: parsed from generated NVDLA_*.h in the nv_small_256 spec/manual directory
method.nvdla_rtl: used to resolve 0-based vs actual counts, byte units, and field positions

C1.shape: FP16 3x3 valid, C16 H8 W8 -> OC32, stride 1

C2.shape: FP16 3x3 valid, C4 H9 W9 -> OC4, stride 1

C3.shape: INT8 quantized 5x5 valid, C8 H8 W8 -> OC32, stride 1

C5.shape: FP16 depthwise 3x3, C3 H11 W28 -> OC3

CNA.question: Is CNA NVDLA CSC + CDMA merged into one target, or a single reorganized CSC?
CNA.answer: Merged, reduced CSC+CDMA register surface - not a single reorganized CSC, and not a copy of either block.
why: CDMA-only functions are present: feature/weight addresses, line/surface strides, fetch grains, CVT.
CSC-only functions are present: dataout size, atomics, weight width/height/kernel extension.
Many CSC/CDMA fields are absent: batch, dilation, right/bottom padding, pixel/image formats, mean, WGS/WMB, second data address, release.
RK adds fields with no NVDLA counterpart: burst lengths, four CVT lanes, CVT_CON5, a packed real-vs-aligned channel pair.
CNA.verdict: reusable with adapter plus specific datapath changes
datapath_changes: CVT path: RK's four scale/offset/truncate lanes and bypass convention (per builder comment) do not match the single integer-only CDMA CVT.
CBUF geometry: RK models 12 banks x 256 entries x 128 B; NVDLA nv_small_256 is 32 banks x 32 B x 128 deep with 256-bit entries. The -1 entry conversion alone does not prove equivalence.
Input stride/addressing: RK DMA_CON1/2 are 32-byte-unit, 4-row-tiled strides, while NVDLA D_LINE/SURF_STRIDE are byte strides for a different decomposition.

Channel contract: RK transports both padded CBUF channels and real weight channels in DATA_SIZE1; NVDLA splits them across D_DATAIN_SIZE_EXT_1 and D_WEIGHT_SIZE_EXT_1 (an adapter can do this, but it is cross-register).
strongest_evidence: DATA_SIZE0=0x00080008 (C1) vs NVDLA 0x00070007; the asymmetric C5 capture 0x001c000b (H=11,W=28) vs 0x000a001b proves the width/height swap and the +1.
WEIGHT_SIZE2=0x03030020 (C1) packs kw=3,kh=3,kernels=32; NVDLA needs D_WEIGHT_SIZE_EXT_0=0x00020002 and D_WEIGHT_SIZE_EXT_1 kernel=31.
DMA_CON1/2 are 32-byte-unit strides (conv_new_clean.py:274-276), while NVDLA line/surface strides are byte-addressed (cdma.v:829-830).
CVT_CON1..4 merge CDMA scale+offset into one word and appear four times; NVDLA has one scale/offset pair.
unresolved: whether NVDLA CSC/CDMA can reproduce RK's 4-row input tiling without new address logic

rows.arithmetic: RK in=((v>>4)&7)=2, proc=((v>>7)&7)=2, conv_mode=0. NVDLA in=[9:8], proc=[13:12]. Literal copy: in=((v>>8)&3)=1 (INT16), proc=((v>>12)&3)=0 (INT8).
rows.note: Same relative offset 0xc as NVDLA CSC D_MISC_CFG, but the precision fields moved. A pure offset alias would run FP16 data as INT16/INT8.

rows.arithmetic: RK v=0x6000b120: bits 12..15=(7+in_c=11)=0xB, bits 29 and 30 set. NVDLA proc_precision is 2 bits [13:12] -> literal 3 (reserved/invalid); bits 29/30 are reserved.
rows.note: The non-aligned small-channel path uses bits 29,30 and [15:12] for RK-specific DMA/ARGB controls (conv_simple.py:403). NVDLA has no corresponding fields. This is a hard counterexample to a bit-identical rename.

rows.expected_raw: CDMA.D_FETCH_GRAIN = 10 (if RK's 11 is an actual row count)
rows.arithmetic: RK v=0xB0 -> field [15:4]=11. NVDLA GRAINS=[11:0] and RTL fetch_grain=GRAINS+1 (CDMA_dc.v:926), so 11 rows -> 10. Literal copy 0xB0 -> 177 grains.
rows.note: RK shifts the field by 4; the NVDLA field has no shift. The exact count convention is not documented by RK; the +1 is established by the NVDLA RTL.
The x field keeps its position; the y field moves from [5:3] to [18:16]. The stride-2 capture (C2b 0x12) would be x=2,y=2; NVDLA expects 0x00020002.

rows.classification: semantics differ (width/height swapped, actual vs last-index)
rows.arithmetic: C1 v=0x00080008: RK width=high16=8, height=low16=8. NVDLA width=[12:0], height=[28:16], both 0-based (datain_width_w=reg+1, CSC_dl.v:890). Expected 0x00070007. Literal copy: width=8, height=0. Supporting C5 v=0x001c000b (W=28,H=11) vs expected 0x000a001b proves the swap.
rows.note: RK packs width in bits 31:16 and height in 15:0 with actual counts; NVDLA packs width low and height high, both 0-based. This is not a rename.

rows.arithmetic: C1 v=0x000f0010: low=16 (aligned data channels) -> NVDLA data channel-1=15; high=15 (real in_c-1) -> NVDLA weight channel ext=15. C2 v=0x00030010 -> data 15, weight 3. C3 v=0x00070010 -> data 15, weight 7. C5 v=0x00020008 -> data 7, weight 2. Literal copy: data channel=16 (one too many); the high half is ignored.
rows.note: This single RK register carries two different NVDLA concepts: the padded CBUF data channel count and the real weight channel count. NVDLA keeps them in separate registers (D_DATAIN_SIZE_EXT_1 and D_WEIGHT_SIZE_EXT_1).

rows.arithmetic: C1 out_w=6, RK v=6; NVDLA dataout_width is 0-based (is_w_end uses >= dataout_width_cmp, CSC_dl.v:2313), expected 5. C5 out_w=26 -> expected 25.
rows.note: RK CNA carries only the output width; the output height is in CORE_DATAOUT_SIZE_0 (already 0-based). A CSC adapter must combine the two blocks' writes.

rows.arithmetic: C1 out_w*out_h=36, RK v=0x24=36; NVDLA data_out_atomic_w=reg2dp_atomics+1 (CSC_sg.v:648), expected 35. C5 26*9=234 -> 233. Literal copy: 36 atoms (one too many).
C1 32 oc * 3*3*16*2 = 9216 bytes. NVDLA weight_bytes is a byte count used as [31:3] 8-byte bursts (CDMA_wt.v:864), no +1. RK 0x2400=9216 matches exactly.
rows.note: A full CDMA+CSC configuration needs the value written to both blocks; RK has one register.

rows.arithmetic: C1 3*3*16*2=288 bytes/kernel, RK 0x120=288; NVDLA byte_per_kernel=reg2dp+1 (CDMA_wt.v:763), expected 287. C3 INT8 5*5*16*1=400 -> 399. C5 3*3*8*2=144 -> 143.
rows.note: The per-kernel byte count is 0-based in NVDLA and actual in RK.

rows.arithmetic: C1 v=0x03030020: kw=(v>>24)=3, kh=(v>>16)=3, kernels=v&0xffff=32. NVDLA width=kw-1=2, height=kh-1=2, kernel=out_c-1=31 (CSC_sg.v:601). Literal copy to EXT_0: width=v&0x1f=0, height=(v>>16)&0x1f=3. C3 0x05050020: kw=kh=5, kernels=32 -> width/height 4, kernel 31; literal width=0, height=5.
rows.note: One RK register carries three actual-count fields that NVDLA splits across two registers with 0-based values. This is the clearest single disproof of a rename.

rows.arithmetic: C1 v=0xB1: data_bank=v&0xf=1, weight_bank=(v>>4)&0xf=11. NVDLA data_bank=[4:0], weight_bank=[20:16]. Literal copy: data_bank=0x11=17 (out of range), weight_bank=0. C5 v=0x1B -> RK data 11, weight 1; literal data 27, weight 0.
rows.note: RK also puts weight_reuse in bit13; NVDLA has it in CSC D_MISC_CFG bit20. Not exercised in the selected captures.

rows.arithmetic: C1 v=4; NVDLA entries=reg+1 (CSC_dl.v:977, CDMA_dc.v:924), expected 3. Literal copy: 4 entries (one too many).
rows.note: RK uses 128-byte CBUF entries (conv_simple.py:23-26); NVDLA nv_small_256 is 32 banks x 32 B x 128 deep with 256-bit entry width (project.vh:11-13,45). The -1 conversion is necessary but not sufficient to prove CBUF equivalence.

rows.classification: semantics differ (enable polarity per RK comment; integer-only CVT)
rows.arithmetic: RK v=0x0B has bit0=1, bit1=1, bit3=1. The RK builder comment names bit0 CVT_BYPASS and bit1 CVT_TYPE; if that comment is correct, NVDLA CVT_EN (bit0) must be 0 for RK bypass, i.e. the polarity is inverted. Even if the comment is wrong, RK bits 1 and 3 have no NVDLA field.
rows.note: NVDLA CDMA CVT is signed integer subtract/multiply/shift/saturate (CDMA_CVT_cell.v:95,107,121,137); enabling it on FP16 data would reinterpret the bit patterns as integers. This is a datapath difference, not just a rename.

rows.arithmetic: RK each v=0x00010000: scale=(v>>16)=1, offset=v&0xffff=0. NVDLA scale and offset are separate 16-bit registers. Literal copy of the 32-bit value: D_CVT_SCALE low16=0 (scale 0), D_CVT_OFFSET low16=0 (offset 0); the RK scale in the high half is lost.
rows.note: RK has four independent scale/offset pairs at 0x1050..0x105c; NVDLA has one. The captured values are all identity. For in_c==1 RK packs four 6-bit truncates into CVT_CON0 (simple_conv.py:567-570), again four lanes vs NVDLA's one.

rows.arithmetic: regcmd value is 0 (placeholder); job.json patch index 18 replaces bits [47:16] with the input buffer DMA address. NVDLA has low/high and a second data address; RK has one 32-bit address.
rows.note: No high-address write; RK DMA addresses are 32-bit in this command encoding.

rows.arithmetic: RK v=0x000f000f: weight burst len [19:16]=15, data burst len [3:0]=15. NVDLA CSC/CDMA headers have no burst-length register; its memory bursts are internal.
rows.note: Performance control only; no correctness mapping.

rows.arithmetic: RK source comment: 'CDMA_DC stride registers are in 32B units' (conv_new_clean.py:274-276). C1 v=0x20=32 -> 1024 B. NVDLA D_LINE_STRIDE is a byte stride; RTL slices [31:3] into 8-byte address units (cdma.v:829-830) and uses grain_addr=fetch_grain*line_stride (dc.v:927). Literal copy: 32 B.
rows.note: For C1 the packed input row is 8*8*2=128 B; RK's 1024 B is 8 rows, not one row. The two addressing decompositions are not interchangeable.

rows.arithmetic: C1 v=0x20=32 -> 1024 B. RK formula width_stride*(in_h-4)=8*4=32 units; C2 9*5=45 (0x2d) -> 1440 B; C5 28*7=196 (0xc4) -> 6272 B. NVDLA SURF_STRIDE is a byte stride. Literal copy: 32 B.
rows.note: The RK surface stride is not the full packed-surface stride (which would be 1024 B for C1 by coincidence); it follows the 4-row tiling formula. Recompute from the RK layout, do not copy.

rows.classification: semantics differ (width/height swapped, actual vs last-index)
rows.arithmetic: C1 v=0x00080008: RK width=high16=8, height=low16=8; NVDLA width=[12:0], height=[28:16], both 0-based (data_width_inc=reg+1, data_height_w=reg+1; CDMA_dc.v:921,923). Expected 0x00070007. C5 v=0x001c000b (W=28,H=11) vs expected 0x000a001b.
rows.note: RK uses in_w/in_h here (source image) and width_stride/in_h in DATA_SIZE0 (padded CBUF). The source uses width_stride for DATA_SIZE0 and in_w for FC_DATA_SIZE0, but all captured cases have width_stride==in_w, so the capture cannot prove which NVDLA block each targets. The split is inferred from the variable names and the CSC/CDMA field roles.

rows.arithmetic: C1 v=0x10=16 (aligned channels); NVDLA data_surface_inc=channel[12:3]+1 (CDMA_dc.v:914), so 16 -> 15. C3 v=0x10=16 -> 15; C5 v=8 -> 7.
rows.note: This is the padded/aligned channel count. The real weight channel count is DATA_SIZE1[31:16], which maps to CSC D_WEIGHT_SIZE_EXT_1, not here. NVDLA separates the two.

rows.expected_raw: CDMA.D_WEIGHT_ADDR_LOW = patched weight buffer address; HIGH = 0
rows.arithmetic: regcmd value is 0 (placeholder); job.json patch index 24 -> weight buffer. NVDLA has weight low/high plus WGS/WMB metadata addresses; RK has one 32-bit address.
rows.note: 'DCOMP' does not imply compression: the builder points it at the plain packed FP16/INT8 weight buffer. NVDLA D_WEIGHT_FORMAT=0 (uncompressed) is the matching default.

rows.expected_raw: no NVDLA register (0x1180 is outside CSC 0x4000-0x4064 and CDMA 0x3000-0x30e8)
rows.arithmetic: C1 v=7; C1b v=0xF; C2 v=0; C3 v=0; C5 v=7. conv_simple sets input_pack_c2-1; conv_new_clean forces 0 for groups==1; simple_conv uses 0xffff only for in_c==1. No consistent NVDLA meaning.
rows.note: The conv_new_clean comment calls it PER_CHANNEL_CVT_EN, but the values track input_pack_c2, not a channel enable mask. This is a good example of why builder comments are not authoritative.

rows.arithmetic: C3 v=0. RK CNA_PAD_CON0 names left/top; NVDLA CSC has left/top, CDMA has left/right/top/bottom. The FP16 builders never write this register.
rows.note: No non-zero padding capture exists; the SAME-padding case is BLOCKED. Do not claim a padding mapping beyond zero.

rows.arithmetic: C3 v=0xffff8080: low16=0x8080 (two INT8 zero-point bytes), high16=0xffff. NVDLA PAD_VALUE is 16 bits. Literal copy to a 16-bit field takes 0x8080; the upper half is outside.
rows.note: simple_conv.py:522 sets 0xffff8080 when kernel>=3 and INPUT_ZERO_POINT==0. The capture cannot distinguish whether NVDLA CSC feature padding or CDMA image padding consumes it; both are candidates.

CORE.question: Is CORE a CACC subset with a fixed offset shift?
CORE.answer: A CACC subset, but not a fixed offset shift. The first three registers are +4 relative to CACC; CLIP is -0x10 relative; 0x3030 is a read-only CACC status offset.
why: DATAOUT_SIZE_0, DATAOUT_SIZE_1 and CLIP_TRUNCATE map bit-for-bit and value-for-value to CACC.
MISC_CFG is repacked: proc_precision moves [10:8] -> [13:12]; bit0 is RK's is_spatial flag, not CACC's direct/Winograd conv_mode; bit1 is an RK-only depthwise enable.
CACC's DATAOUT_ADDR/BATCH/LINE/SURF/DATAOUT_MAP are absent from RK CORE; RK has a compacted map.
0x3030 collides with CACC D_OUT_SATURATION, which is read-only.
CORE.verdict: reusable with a pure register adapter (for the accumulator/output-size subset)
datapath_changes: Repack MISC_CFG precision and drop the RK spatial/depthwise bits.
If the CACC memory-write path is used, synthesize D_DATAOUT_ADDR and the line/surface strides; RK does not provide them.
Do not forward 0x3030 as a control; it is a read-only CACC status offset.
strongest_evidence: DATAOUT_SIZE_0=0x00050005 and DATAOUT_SIZE_1=0x1F match CACC exactly (0-based W/H/C).
MISC_CFG=0x201 for a direct 3x3 conv would be CACC conv_mode=1 (Winograd) and proc=0 if copied literally.
CLIP at 0x301c vs CACC 0x702c disproves a single fixed offset shift.
unresolved: whether the RK CORE actually has a memory-write port

rows.classification: repacked bits + semantics differ (bit0=spatial, not conv_mode)
rows.arithmetic: C1 v=0x201: RK proc=(v>>8)&3=2, spatial=v&1=1, dw=(v>>1)&1=0. NVDLA proc=[13:12], conv_mode=bit0. Expected 0x2000. Literal copy: conv_mode=1 (Winograd), proc=((v>>12)&3)=0 (INT8).
rows.note: conv_new_clean.py:572-574 sets bit0=is_spatial for every 3x3/5x5 conv; the comment 'OPERATION_ENABLE' is misleading. A literal copy would run every spatial conv as NVDLA Winograd. C3 v=0x001 and C5 v=0x203 also set bit0=1.

rows.arithmetic: C3 v=0x001: RK proc=0 (INT8), spatial=1. Expected conv_mode=0, proc=0 -> 0x0000. Literal copy: conv_mode=1.
rows.note: The INT8 case confirms bit0 is the spatial flag, not an operation enable.

rows.arithmetic: C1 out 6x6: RK ((out_h-1)<<16) + (out_w-1) = (5<<16)+5 = 0x00050005. NVDLA width=[12:0], height=[28:16], both 0-based. Literal copy is exact. C5 9x26 -> 0x00080019, also exact.
rows.note: This is one of the genuinely reusable CACC fields.

rows.arithmetic: C1 align_out_c=32 -> out_channel_field=31. NVDLA channel field is 0-based; literal copy is exact. C3 and C5 also write 31.
rows.note: The real out_c-1 (e.g. 3 for C2) is only in DPU DATA_CUBE_CHANNEL[31:16]; NVDLA CACC has one channel field.

rows.arithmetic: C3 v=0. RK relative offset 0x1c; NVDLA CACC D_CLIP_CFG relative 0x2c. Literal copy of 0 is exact.
rows.note: The previous REFERENCE_MAPPING's '+4 shift' holds for MISC/DATAOUT_SIZE_0/1 but not for CLIP (0x301c vs 0x702c). The CORE map is compacted, not uniformly shifted.

rows.expected_raw: no writable NVDLA field; D_OUT_SATURATION is read-only status
rows.classification: RK-only (NVDLA read-only at the same relative offset)
rows.arithmetic: C1 v=0. NVDLA CACC 0x7030 is D_OUT_SATURATION, driven by dp2reg_sat_count (CACC_regfile.v:16,41,200); there is no d0/d1 writable field.
rows.note: A bridge write of 0 here is harmless but has no NVDLA function. RK calls it RESERVED/clear-stale-state.

DPU.question: Map the DPU fields to NVDLA SDP D_* fields.
DPU.answer: Same SDP BS/BN/EW datapath family, but a repacked control surface. Cube dimensions and several bypass/CVT fields map cleanly; FEATURE_MODE_CFG, DATA_FORMAT and EW_CFG do not.
why: DATA_CUBE_WIDTH/HEIGHT and the low channel field are exact 0-based aliases.
BS_CFG=0x53 and BN_CFG=0x53 are bit-identical to SDP D_DP_BS_CFG/D_DP_BN_CFG bypass layouts.
OUT_CVT_OFFSET/SHIFT/SCALE map to SDP D_CVT_OFFSET/SHIFT/SCALE (scale low 16 bits).
FEATURE_MODE_CFG packs burst/conv/output mode into bits that SDP reads as Winograd/batch.
DATA_FORMAT has an RK-only IN_PRECISION and a 3-bit OUT_PRECISION; SDP has 2-bit PROC/OUT only.
EW_CFG uses a 3-bit ALU opcode at [18:16], a separate MUL select, and SUB/FDIV opcodes that SDP's EW ALU does not have.
DPU.verdict: reusable with adapter plus specific datapath changes (EW stage is compile-time disabled in nv_small_256)
DPU.build_caveat: nv_small_256 has NVDLA_SDP_EW_THROUGHPUT=0 (project.vh:16); NV_NVDLA_SDP_core.v ties cfg_ew_en to 0 (lines 329,334) and has no reg2dp_ew_* ports; NV_NVDLA_sdp.v ties the WDMA EW config to ew_bypass=1 (lines 260-262). The EW register definitions exist in the header, but the EW datapath is not usable in this reference build.
datapath_changes: EW datapath enablement: nv_small_256 compiles the SDP EW stage out (NVDLA_SDP_EW_THROUGHPUT=0, cfg_ew_en tied 0). Reusing the reference RTL for RK EW requires enabling/instantiating the EW stage, not just programming D_DP_EW_CFG. If that integration is out of scope, RK EW is not reusable without new RTL.

CORE->DPU feed: the conv streams write no RDMA source address and DPU flying_mode=0, so DPU must be fed by CORE. NVDLA SDP has no CACC->SDP path; use a CACC memory round-trip (requires CACC output address/strides) or add a direct feed.
EW ALU: ADD/MAX/MUL/NEG are adapter-mappable; SUB needs operand negation (not proven) and FDIV needs a divider that SDP does not have.
FP32 output: RK's 1x1 FP16 path uses OUT_PRECISION=5; SDP's 2-bit field cannot encode it.
NC1HWC2 surface addressing: RK's DST_SURF_STRIDE is an 8-channel plane stride (padded to 4 atoms); SDP needs DST_LINE_STRIDE synthesized and its surface granularity validated.
BS_OW_CFG/WDMA_SIZE/SURFACE_ADD are RK-only; the adapter must translate or drop them consistently.
strongest_evidence: FEATURE_MODE_CFG=0x1E5 decodes in SDP as flying=1, winograd=1, batch=1, but RK means output_mode=2 and burst=15.
EW_CFG=0x108402C0 for SUB has ALU_ALGO=4 at [18:16]; SDP's 2-bit ALU_ALGO at [3:2] cannot represent it and has no SUB enum.
DATA_FORMAT=0x48000002 decodes in SDP as proc=FP16, out=INT8; the RK out=FP16 is at [31:29], not [3:2].
DATA_FORMAT=0xA8000002 uses OUT_PRECISION=5 (FP32), which SDP cannot represent.

nv_small_256 disables the SDP EW stage at compile time: NVDLA_SDP_EW_THROUGHPUT=0, cfg_ew_en=0, and the core has no reg2dp_ew_* ports. RK's EW ops therefore cannot run on this reference build without enabling the EW datapath.
unresolved: whether SDP's EW ALU can implement SUB by operand negation

rows.expected_raw: Not forwardable; NVDLA S_POINTER is a shadow-group selector
rows.arithmetic: RK v=0xE sets bits1,2,3 (PP_MODE, EXECUTER_PP_EN, POINTER_PP_EN). NVDLA PRODUCER=bit0, CONSUMER=bit16; literal 0xE decodes to producer=0, consumer=0 (both d0).
rows.note: The bridge must implement NVDLA's d0/d1 producer-consumer commit protocol; it cannot forward RK's PP bits.

rows.arithmetic: RK C4 v=0x1E5: flying=bit0=1, output_mode=(v>>1)&3=2, conv_mode=(v>>3)&3=0, burst=(v>>5)&0xF=15. NVDLA flying=bit0, output_dst=bit1, winograd=bit2, nan=bit3, batch=[12:8]. Literal copy: flying=1, output_dst=0, winograd=1, nan=0, batch=(v>>8)&0x1F=1 (2 batches). C1 conv v=0x1E4: literal flying=0, winograd=1, batch=1.
rows.note: RK OUTPUT_MODE=2 sets bit2, which NVDLA reads as WINOGRAD. RK BURST_LEN=15<<5 sets bit8, which NVDLA reads as batch_number=1. Neither field has an SDP counterpart. A literal copy is wrong.

rows.arithmetic: C1 v=0x48000002: RK proc=v&3=2, in=(v>>26)&7=2, out=(v>>29)&7=2. NVDLA proc=[1:0], out=[3:2]. Expected 0x0A. Literal copy: proc=2, out=(v>>2)&3=0 (INT8 output).
rows.note: NVDLA SDP has no in_precision; it is in SDP_RDMA D_FEATURE_MODE_CFG[3:2]. C1b v=0xA8000002 has RK out=5 (FP32); NVDLA SDP's 2-bit OUT_PRECISION cannot encode 5. FP32 output is RK-only.

rows.expected_raw: SDP.D_DST_BASE_ADDR_LOW = patched output buffer address; HIGH = 0
rows.arithmetic: regcmd value 0 (placeholder); job.json patch index 32 -> out buffer. NVDLA has low/high plus line/surface/batch strides; RK has one 32-bit base and a surface stride.

rows.expected_raw: SDP.D_DST_SURFACE_STRIDE = 576 (C1, candidate); 1152 if the NVDLA surface is 16 FP16 channels
rows.arithmetic: C1 v=0x240=576 = out_width_stride<<4 = 36*16 = 6*6*8*2 (one 8-channel NC1HWC2 plane). C2 v=0x340=832 = 52*16, while W*H*8*2=784; RK pads the plane atom count to a multiple of 4. C5 v=0xEC0=3776 vs 26*9*8*2=3744.
rows.note: NVDLA's DST_SURFACE_STRIDE is a byte stride. The adapter must also synthesize DST_LINE_STRIDE = out_w*8*2 (RK never writes it). The value matches an 8-channel plane for C1/C3, but NV_NVDLA_SDP_WDMA_cmd.v:155 says 'Surf is always in unit of ATOMIC (1x1x32B)', i.e. 16 FP16 channels; in that case the candidate is 2x = 1152 (which equals RK's SURFACE_ADD). The reference build's surface grouping must be resolved by simulation.

rows.arithmetic: C1 out_w=6 -> RK 5; NVDLA width is 0-based (cfg_mode_1x1_pack uses width==0, WDMA_cmd.v:146; is_last_w at 210). C4 EW n=8 -> RK 0; NVDLA 0. Literal copy is exact.
rows.note: For EW, RK's width is the number of 8-lane columns minus 1 (elementwise.py:296); NVDLA's width is cube columns, so the same value describes the same padded cube when channel=7.

rows.arithmetic: C1 out_h=6 -> RK 5; NVDLA height is 0-based (is_last_h=count_h==size_of_height, WDMA_cmd.v:231). C4 EW height 0. Literal copy is exact.
C1 v=0. The low-12 offset 0x38 collides with NVDLA SDP D_OP_ENABLE at 0x9038; a naive alias would write OP_EN=0.
rows.note: RK requires this to be 0; NVDLA derives the cube shape from W/H/C and has no notch control.

rows.classification: repacked bits (low field identical; high 16 RK-only)
rows.arithmetic: C1 v=0x001F001F: low=align_out_c-1=31, high=out_c-1=31. NVDLA channel=[12:0], 0-based; literal low is exact. C2 v=0x0003001F: low=31 (padded 32), high=3 (real 4). C4 v=0x00070007: low=7, high=7.
rows.note: NVDLA has one channel field. For C2 the low 31 requests 32 padded channels, matching the 32-channel output BO; the high half is RK metadata.

rows.classification: renamed/relocated for 0x53; repacked + RK-only high bits for INT8 0x20150
rows.arithmetic: C1 v=0x53 = bits 0,1,4,6 -> exactly NVDLA BS_BYPASS/ALU_BYPASS/MUL_BYPASS/RELU_BYPASS; literal copy is exact. C3 v=0x20150 = bits 4,6,8,17; bits 8 and 17 are outside D_DP_BS_CFG[6:0]. Literal copy: BS_BYPASS=0, ALU_BYPASS=0, ALU_ALGO=0 (MAX), MUL_BYPASS=1, RELU_BYPASS=1.
rows.note: The low 7 bits match the NVDLA layout. The INT8 builder adds undocumented bits 8 and 17 (simple_conv.py:598). Do not assume they are NVDLA fields.

rows.arithmetic: C1 v=0x126 = (1<<8)+(1<<5)+(1<<2)+(1<<1): SIZE_E_2[9:8], SIZE_E_1[6:5], SIZE_E_0[3:2], OD_BYPASS bit1. C5 v=0x36E uses 3 in all size fields. The low-12 offset 0x50 collides with D_DST_LINE_STRIDE at 0x9050.
rows.note: NVDLA SDP has no output-width/size-E control; its operand widths are fixed by D_DATA_FORMAT. A naive alias would write 0x126 as the destination line stride.

rows.arithmetic: C1 v=0x1F=31 (aligned channel-1), same as DATA_CUBE_CHANNEL low. The low-12 offset 0x58 collides with D_DP_BS_CFG at 0x9058; a naive write of 0x1F would set BS bypass/ALU/MUL/RELU bits.
rows.note: The adapter can drop this if it is consistent with DATA_CUBE_CHANNEL.

rows.arithmetic: C1 v=0x00050005 = ((out_h-1)<<16) + (out_w-1), same as the cube dims. The low-12 offset 0x5c collides with D_DP_BS_ALU_CFG at 0x905c.
rows.note: Drop if consistent with the cube dims.

rows.arithmetic: C1 v=0x53 = bits 0,1,4,6, exactly the NVDLA BN bypass layout. Literal copy is exact. C3 also writes 0x53.

rows.classification: repacked bits + semantics differ (opcode width/values, SUB/FDIV absent)
rows.arithmetic: ADD v=0x108202c0: ALU_ALGO=(v>>16)&7=2, OP_TYPE=bit2=0, OP_SRC=bit6=1, LUT_BYPASS=bit7=1, REL=bit9=1. NVDLA ALU_ALGO=[3:2] 2 bits; literal (v>>2)&3=0 (MAX), not SUM. SUB v=0x108402c0: ALU_ALGO=4 -> cannot fit NVDLA's 2-bit field. MUL v=0x108003c4: OP_TYPE=1 -> NVDLA literal ALU_ALGO=(v>>2)&3=1 (MIN); NVDLA uses a separate EW_MUL block. MAX v=0x108002c0: literal ALU_ALGO=0 (MAX) coincides, but MUL_BYPASS=0 leaves the MUL active.
rows.note: NVDLA SDP EW ALU supports MAX/MIN/SUM (2-bit, HLS_X_int_alu.v:105-110; enum EQL is treated as SUM). RK has a 3-bit ALU_ALGO at [18:16] with MAX=0, ADD=2, FDIV=3, SUB=4 and selects MUL via OP_TYPE bit2. ADD/MAX/MUL/NEG are adapter-mappable; SUB needs operand negation (not proven); FDIV has no NVDLA divider.

rows.classification: renamed/relocated (one RK value -> two NVDLA registers)
rows.arithmetic: C1 v=1. RK has one scale value; NVDLA has separate ALU and MUL CVT scale/offset/truncate registers. Literal copy of 1 to either is exact.
rows.note: The captured cases only need identity scale; NVDLA offsets/truncates default to 0.

rows.arithmetic: C1 v=0x00010001: low16=1 -> NVDLA CVT_SCALE=1; bit16=FP32TOFP16_EN has no NVDLA field. C3 v=0x00004041: low16=0x4041 -> NVDLA CVT_SCALE=0x4041. Literal low16 is exact.
rows.note: NVDLA SDP has separate D_CVT_OFFSET (0x90c0) and D_CVT_SHIFT (0x90c8); RK writes them at 0x4080/0x4088 in the INT8 case. For FP16, NVDLA output precision is controlled by D_DATA_FORMAT OUT_PRECISION; RK's bit16 is explicit.

rows.arithmetic: C1 v=0x480=1152 = (out_width_stride * max(2,align_out_c/16))<<4 = 36*2*16. In all captured cases align_out_c=32, so SURFACE_ADD = 2 * DST_SURF_STRIDE: C1 2*576=1152, C2 2*832=1664, C3 2*256=512, C5 2*3776=7552.
rows.note: NVDLA has no surface-add; it uses DST_LINE/SURFACE/BATCH_STRIDE. SURFACE_ADD = 2*DST_SURF_STRIDE in all captured cases, so if NVDLA's surface is 16 FP16 channels (1x1x32B), SURFACE_ADD is the closer candidate for D_DST_SURFACE_STRIDE and DST_SURF_STRIDE is the 8-channel sub-surface stride. This is unresolved.

rows.arithmetic: C3 v=0xFFFFFF80 (signed -128). NVDLA D_CVT_OFFSET is 32-bit; literal copy is exact.
rows.note: Only the INT8 builder writes this.

rows.arithmetic: C3 v=0x16=22. NVDLA D_CVT_SHIFT is [5:0]; literal copy is exact.
rows.note: Only the INT8 builder writes this.

RDMA.question: Map S_POINTER, CUBE_*, SRC_BASE, ERDMA_CFG, EW_BASE, FEATURE_MODE_CFG to NVDLA SDP_RDMA.
RDMA.answer: SDP_RDMA family. Four fields are exact aliases (cube W/H/C and SRC_BASE low); the rest are relocated/repacked, and one field has no counterpart.
why: RK 0x500c/0x5010/0x5014/0x5018 are the same low-12 offsets as SDP_RDMA D_DATA_CUBE_WIDTH/HEIGHT/CHANNEL and D_SRC_BASE_ADDR_LOW, with the same 0-based/byte encodings.
ERDMA_CFG moves data_mode to bit30 and uses bits[3:2] for data_size; SDP_RDMA uses bit4 and bit3.
FEATURE_MODE_CFG puts in_precision at [16:15] and proc_precision at [6:5]; SDP_RDMA uses [3:2] and [5:4], and bits 11-14 collide with batch_number.
RDMA_WEIGHT 0x5068 has no SDP_RDMA control; its low-12 offset collides with D_EW_SURFACE_STRIDE.
RK does not write SRC/BS/EW line/surface/batch strides, which SDP_RDMA needs for general tensors.
The nv_small_256 build does not instantiate ERDMA and hardwires erdma_disable=1, so the EW operand read path used by the captured FP16 EW cases is absent from the reference RTL.
RDMA.verdict: adapter + datapath change for the captured FP16 EW cases (ERDMA is not instantiated in nv_small_256); adapter + config addition for the INT8 BRDMA bias path; pure adapter only for the MRDMA cube/source fields
RDMA.build_caveat: nv_small_256 has NVDLA_SDP_EW_THROUGHPUT=0 (project.vh:16). NV_NVDLA_SDP_rdma.v hardwires erdma_disable=1 (line 350) and instantiates only BRDMA/NRDMA (lines 216,258); there is no u_erdma instance and NV_NVDLA_sdp.v connects no sdp_erdma2dp_* signals. The ERDMA register definitions exist in the header, but the EW operand read path is absent from this build.
datapath_changes: ERDMA enablement: nv_small_256 does not instantiate the ERDMA block and hardwires erdma_disable=1. RK's FP16 EW cases use ERDMA_CFG/EW_BASE to fetch the B operand, so reusing this reference RTL for those cases requires enabling/instantiating ERDMA, not just repacking fields. If that is out of scope, the captured EW path is not reusable without new RTL.
For captured EW: repack ERDMA_CFG/FEATURE_MODE_CFG, set ERDMA data_use from the DPU op, and default the three EW strides to 0 (1x1x8 tensor).
For INT8 conv: RDMA_WEIGHT 0x5068 is unmappable; the bias path also needs BS strides, and the BRDMA data_size for int32 bias is unproven.
For general tensors: synthesize SRC/BS/EW line/surface/batch strides; RK does not carry them.
strongest_evidence: Cube W/H/C and SRC_BASE low are exact aliases (0x500c/10/14/18 -> 0x800c/10/14/18).
FEATURE_MODE_CFG=0x17849 copies into SDP_RDMA as proc_precision=0 and batch_number=24; RK means proc=FP16 and burst=15.
ERDMA_CFG=0x40000008 copies as data_use=MUL and data_mode=0; RK means data_mode=1 and the EW operand is used by the ALU for ADD/SUB/MAX.
RDMA_WEIGHT=0x01010101 has no SDP_RDMA register and is nonsensical as EW_SURFACE_STRIDE.
The reference RTL cannot execute the captured EW operand fetch: NV_NVDLA_SDP_rdma.v sets erdma_disable=1 and has no u_erdma instance.
unresolved: which RK register is the EW surface stride (0x5040 vs 0x5068)
enabling/instantiating ERDMA in the reference build

rows.note: The bridge must implement the d0/d1 commit protocol; RK's PP bits cannot be forwarded.

rows.arithmetic: C4 n=8 -> RK 0; NVDLA width 0-based (cfg_mode_1x1_pack at MRDMA_ig.v:192, is_last_w at 253). Literal copy is exact. C3 out 4x4 -> RK 3; NVDLA 3.
rows.note: One of the few exact aliases: RK 0x500c -> NVDLA 0x800c.

rows.arithmetic: C4 height 0; NVDLA 0-based (is_last_h=count_h==height, MRDMA_ig.v:253). C3 4x4 -> 3. Literal copy is exact.
rows.note: Exact alias: RK 0x5010 -> NVDLA 0x8010.

rows.arithmetic: C4 8 lanes -> RK 7; NVDLA channel 0-based (size_of_surf=channel[12:3], MRDMA_ig.v:204-208). C3 32 channels -> 31. Literal copy is exact.
rows.note: Exact alias: RK 0x5014 -> NVDLA 0x8014.

rows.expected_raw: SDP_RDMA.D_SRC_BASE_ADDR_LOW = patched a buffer address; HIGH = 0
rows.arithmetic: regcmd value 0 (placeholder); job.json patch index 15 -> a buffer. RK 0x5018 -> NVDLA 0x8018 low; high 0x801c is not written.
rows.note: The low-half offset is an exact alias. RK has no high-address write.

rows.arithmetic: C4 v=0x40000008: RK data_size=2<<2 (bit3=1), data_mode=bit30=1, disable=bit0=0. NVDLA disable=bit0, data_use=[2:1], data_size=bit3, data_mode=bit4, ram=bit5. Literal copy: disable=0, data_use=(v>>1)&3=0 (MUL), data_size=1, data_mode=(v>>4)&1=0. C3 v=1: literal disable=1 (plausible: no EW operand in the bias-only conv).
rows.note: The adapter must move bit30->bit4 and set data_use=1 for ADD/SUB/MAX (ALU), or 0 for MUL/NEG. The captured EW value cannot be copied literally. nv_small_256 does not instantiate ERDMA, so this field has no usable datapath in the reference build.

rows.expected_raw: SDP_RDMA.D_EW_BASE_ADDR_LOW = patched b buffer address; HIGH = 0
rows.arithmetic: regcmd value 0 (placeholder); job.json patch index 16 -> b buffer. RK 0x5038 -> NVDLA 0x805c low; offset is not an alias (0x38 vs 0x5c).
rows.note: NVDLA also needs EW_LINE_STRIDE (0x8064), EW_SURFACE_STRIDE (0x8068) and EW_BATCH_STRIDE (0x806c); RK writes none in the captured EW cases. For a 1x1x8 vector, zero strides are a plausible default, but this is not proven.

rows.classification: repacked bits + collisions; RK-only BURST_LEN and FP16TOFP32 bits
rows.arithmetic: C4 v=0x00017849: flying=bit0=1, in_prec=2<<15 (bit16), proc_prec=2<<5 (bit6), burst=15<<11, fp16tofp32=bit3. NVDLA flying=bit0, winograd=bit1, in=[3:2], proc=[5:4], out=[7:6], batch=[12:8]. Literal copy: flying=1, in=(v>>2)&3=2, proc=(v>>4)&3=0, out=(v>>6)&3=1, batch=(v>>8)&0x1f=24. C3 v=0x7810 -> literal proc=1, out=0, batch=24.
rows.note: RK's proc field at bit5/6 collides with NVDLA out_precision; the 15<<11 burst field sets batch_number=24 if copied. The adapter must take precision from DPU DATA_FORMAT/RK FEATURE_MODE and drop burst/fp16tofp32.

rows.arithmetic: C3 v=2 -> NVDLA bit1 = BRDMA_DATA_USE=1 (ALU), disable=0. Literal copy is exact for those two bits. The captured value also leaves BRDMA_DATA_SIZE=0 (one byte) and BRDMA_DATA_MODE=0 (per-kernel); whether those are correct for int32 bias is not resolved.
rows.note: The INT8 bias is int32 in the source (simple_conv.py:618 BS_BASE_ADDR); NVDLA BRDMA data_size=0 means one byte. Whether NVDLA BRDMA must be configured for 4-byte bias is not resolved by the capture. RK writes no BS line/surface strides.

rows.expected_raw: SDP_RDMA.D_BS_BASE_ADDR_LOW = patched bias buffer address; HIGH = 0
rows.arithmetic: regcmd value 0 (placeholder); job.json patch index 61 -> bias buffer. RK 0x5020 -> NVDLA 0x802c low.
rows.note: NVDLA also needs BS_LINE_STRIDE/SURFACE_STRIDE/BATCH_STRIDE; RK writes none in the captured case.

rows.expected_raw: no matching SDP_RDMA control; offset 0x5068 collides with D_EW_SURFACE_STRIDE at 0x8068
rows.arithmetic: C3 v=0x01010101 = four bytes of 0x01. NVDLA D_EW_SURFACE_STRIDE would be 16,843,009 bytes, nonsensical for a 4x4x32 output. The source comment is only 'RDMA weight config' (simple_conv.py:621).
rows.note: This is the strongest RDMA unmappable field. It may be a per-channel weight/scale config, but the available sources do not define it. Do not invent a mapping.

summary.strict_hypothesis_reason: No consistent offset alias exists; only 4 RDMA fields are identical aliases. CNA/CORE/DPU/RDMA fields are repacked with different value conventions, and several fields have no counterpart.
summary.weaker_hypothesis: consistent with NVDLA-derived blocks and a rewritten register file, but register streams cannot prove RTL identity
